full.text: DNA replicates by the semi-conservative method: each new molecule has one original strand and one new strand. Meselson and Stahl showed this with heavy nitrogen (15N).

items: Helicase unwinds the double helix and breaks hydrogen bonds between bases
Free nucleotides pair with exposed bases: A with T, C with G
DNA polymerase joins nucleotides in the 5' to 3' direction
The leading strand is made continuously; the lagging strand is made in Okazaki fragments joined by DNA ligase
A short RNA primer is needed to start each new strand

full.text: Each daughter DNA molecule contains one parental strand and one newly made strand.

full.title: Past-paper tip
full.text: DNA polymerase can only add nucleotides to the 3' end of a growing strand. This explains why the lagging strand is discontinuous.

items: Semi-conservative (Meselson and Stahl)
Helicase unwinds, breaks H bonds
Complementary pairing A-T, C-G
DNA polymerase works 5' to 3'
Leading strand continuous; lagging strand Okazaki fragments
DNA ligase joins fragments

full.text: The making of an RNA copy of a gene, using one DNA strand as a template.

items: RNA polymerase binds to the *promoter* and unwinds the DNA
Free RNA nucleotides pair with the template strand: A with U, T with A, C with G
RNA polymerase joins them to form pre-mRNA, 5' to 3'
Transcription stops at a terminator sequence

full.text: In eukaryotes the pre-mRNA is processed in the nucleus: introns are removed by splicing, a 5' cap and poly-A tail are added, and the mature mRNA leaves through a nuclear pore.

full.title: Past-paper tip
full.text: Uracil replaces thymine in RNA. Questions often ask you to write the mRNA sequence from a template strand.

items: RNA polymerase binds promoter
Template strand read; uracil pairs with adenine
Pre-mRNA made 5' to 3'
Eukaryotes: introns removed, cap and poly-A tail added
mRNA leaves nucleus via pores

full.text: Recombinant DNA joins DNA from different sources, often to make a genetically modified organism.

items: Restriction enzymes cut DNA at specific recognition sequences, often leaving *sticky ends*
The same enzyme cuts the *vector*, such as a bacterial plasmid
DNA ligase joins the gene into the vector
The recombinant plasmid is put into host cells (transformation)
Cells that took up the plasmid are selected using marker genes, such as antibiotic resistance

full.text: A DNA molecule, such as a plasmid or virus, used to carry a foreign gene into a host cell.
The human insulin gene inserted into bacteria lets them make human insulin for people with diabetes.

full.title: Past-paper tip
full.text: Name both enzymes: restriction endonuclease to cut, DNA ligase to join.

items: Restriction enzymes cut; sticky ends
Vector: plasmid or virus
DNA ligase joins gene and vector
Transformation of host cells
Marker genes to select
Example: human insulin from bacteria

written.stem: Describe the process of DNA replication.
written.model_answer: Helicase unwinds DNA and breaks hydrogen bonds. Free nucleotides pair with complementary bases on each template strand. DNA polymerase joins them 5' to 3'. The lagging strand forms Okazaki fragments that DNA ligase joins. Each new molecule has one old and one new strand (semi-conservative).

written.stem: Explain how mRNA is formed during transcription in a eukaryotic cell.
written.model_answer: RNA polymerase binds to the promoter and unwinds the DNA. RNA nucleotides pair with the template strand with uracil opposite adenine and are joined to form pre-mRNA. Introns are removed by splicing and the mature mRNA leaves the nucleus.

points.text: Template strand, complementary pairing with uracil

written.stem: Outline the steps used to produce human insulin using bacteria.
written.model_answer: The insulin gene is cut out with a restriction enzyme. A plasmid is cut with the same enzyme. DNA ligase joins the gene into the plasmid. The recombinant plasmid is taken up by bacteria, which are selected with marker genes and grown to produce insulin.

written.stem: Explain the principle of the polymerase chain reaction (PCR).
written.model_answer: DNA is heated to about 95 C to separate the strands; it is cooled to about 55 C so primers anneal; then at about 72 C a heat-stable DNA polymerase (Taq) extends the primers. The cycle is repeated, doubling the DNA each time.

written.stem: Describe how a polypeptide is made at a ribosome during translation.
written.model_answer: mRNA attaches to the small ribosomal subunit and the start codon AUG is found. A tRNA with the complementary anticodon brings methionine. The next tRNA binds the next codon, and a peptide bond forms between the amino acids. The ribosome moves along one codon at a time, releasing tRNAs, until a stop codon is reached and the polypeptide is released.

points.text: mRNA binds ribosome, start codon AUG

written.stem: Discuss the benefits and concerns of genetically modified organisms.
written.model_answer: Benefits include crops with higher yield, pest resistance (Bt crops), herbicide tolerance and better nutrition (Golden Rice), and microbes that make medicines such as insulin. Concerns include gene flow to wild relatives, effects on non-target organisms, reduced biodiversity, possible allergies, and ethical and economic issues such as seed patents.

ask.question: Why is DNA replication called semi-conservative?
ask.answer: Each new DNA molecule contains one strand from the original molecule and one newly made strand. Meselson and Stahl showed this using DNA labelled with heavy nitrogen.

sources.title: A/L Biology syllabus (2025), topic 7.2: DNA replication

ask.question: What happens during transcription?
ask.answer: RNA polymerase binds to the promoter, unwinds the DNA and builds an mRNA copy of one template strand using complementary base pairing, with uracil instead of thymine. In eukaryotes introns are then removed.

ask.question: What is a codon?
ask.answer: A codon is a sequence of three bases on mRNA that codes for one amino acid or a stop signal. AUG is the start codon.

sources.title: A/L Biology syllabus (2025), topic 7.4: Translation and the genetic code

ask.question: What is recombinant DNA?
ask.answer: Recombinant DNA is DNA made by joining DNA from different sources. A gene is cut with a restriction enzyme, inserted into a vector such as a plasmid with DNA ligase, and transferred into a host cell.

sources.title: A/L Biology syllabus (2025), topic 7.7: Recombinant DNA technology

ask.question: What is PCR used for?
ask.answer: PCR makes millions of copies of a chosen DNA sequence by repeated cycles of heating, primer annealing and extension by a heat-stable DNA polymerase. It is used in forensics, diagnosis and research.
